title: The popular version. Duolingo is a free app for learning languages.
description:
Duolingo is a free app for learning languages. It is. But it was built to make money another way.

The idea came from Carnegie Mellon. Von Ahn had already worked on reCAPTCHA, which used people to digitise books.

Learners translate real web articles. The translations were then sold to media companies.

CNN and BuzzFeed. BuzzFeed's system sent an article to Duolingo once it became popular enough.

More than this many a day were translated by students, according to a report from April 2014.

Other income replaced it. The English test, advertising and subscriptions took over the translation service.

The lessons were the product. The learners were the workforce.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duolingo (read): idea formulated in 2009 by Carnegie Mellon professor Luis von Ahn and his student Severin Hacker; private beta launched on 30 November 2011 in the body (27 November in the infobox), public launch 19 June 2012; early revenue came from a crowdsourced translation service, later replaced by the Duolingo English Test, advertising and subscriptions (no date given).
- https://gmrtranscription.com/blog/duolingo-finalize-translation-deals-buzzfeed-cnn (read): dated 2 April 2014; BuzzFeed's publishing system automatically sends an article to Duolingo after a certain point of fame; CNN staff send articles to volunteers; students do the translating as part of learning; more than 30 articles translated by students daily.
- https://curiouspm.substack.com/p/duolingo-the-backstory (read): the plan was to teach a language for free, have users translate online articles as part of the teaching, and sell the translations to media houses; names CNN and BuzzFeed as deals.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReCAPTCHA (read): von Ahn was among reCAPTCHA's developers at Carnegie Mellon; it paired a known word with an uncertain scanned word to digitise books; a cited source dated 16 September 2009 is titled "Teaching computers to read: Google acquires reCAPTCHA".
